hypothesis: The node-11 failure is not due to the chosen idea itself but to a train_lib torch-model implementation bug: with multitask='aux_click_like_forward', the library builds an nn.ModuleDict of auxiliary heads keyed by task name, and one key is 'forward', which collides with nn.Module.forward and raises KeyError("attribute 'forward' already exists"). To preserve the original intent as closely as possible, I keep the deep candidate-aware history model (deepfm_mlp + din_attention), ranking-aligned BPR loss, recency prior, and lower-lr schedule, but drop the incompatible multitask setting to 'none'. This isolates the bug while still testing whether DIN-style query-dependent history with an MLP scorer can improve within-user ranking over FM. If DIN helps top-of-list personalization, nDCG@5 should rise even without the auxiliary tasks; if not, this also cleanly tells us the prior gain came mostly from FM-side signals rather than the torch architecture.
expected_effect: Bug fix: should run successfully instead of crashing. Relative to node 10, I expect this DIN+DeepFM variant without aux tasks to land roughly between -0.002 and +0.002 primary; central estimate 0.6035 valid primary, with upside mainly via +0.001 to +0.003 nDCG@5 if candidate-aware history beats mean pooling.
